exposure: Source-informed acquisition diagnostics written after reading the governing archive and before running this comparison. These are not held-out problems and are not implementation fixtures or query aliases.

cases.query: I have an explicit Boolean cubic with a hidden truncated extension-field structure. Can I recover the ring and affine center instead of receiving their coordinates from an oracle?
There are many repeated cubic pairs, so enumerating every residue value is too expensive. Can a fixed number of low-degree point counts replace that field scan?
Does a radical-free cubic with a fully acquired scalar centroid guarantee only finitely many nondegenerate critical rays for exact counting?
An ordinary Artin-Schreier hypersurface callback returns its number of rational points. How do I convert that cardinality to the signed character moment without a factor-of-two error?
I need to bound how many binary-independent solutions a coordinatewise squaring equation with an invertible field matrix can have, independently of the extension degree.
Can the repeated-pair counting result ignore its field degree restriction when arbitrary higher nilpotent cubic coefficients are added?
My coefficient algebra has a nilpotent ideal. Is reducing to its residue field enough to use an extension-field quadratic-defect decoder without losing the counting phase?
Where is the measured practical speed advantage of an implemented general polynomial-time point-counting engine for these acquired ring counters?
